observation_boundary: Remote web pages are recorded as dated observations in findings inputs; their page bytes are not archived or content-hashed by this projection.

research_sources.finding: AISI states that Inspect powers many of its frontier evaluations; it reports METR migrated its time-horizon evaluations to Inspect and that Apollo Research builds new evaluations on Inspect. These are AISI-reported adoption statements, not independent comparative measurements.
research_sources.title: Releasing AISI's Engineering Playbook

research_sources.finding: Apalache is a symbolic TLA+ model checker using SMT solving for finite, bounded executions; its own documentation calls it experimental and describes TLC as mature.
research_sources.title: Apalache documentation

research_sources.finding: The PyPI project lists ArviZ 1.3.0; the project describes posterior analysis, model checking, comparison, and diagnostics for Bayesian models.
research_sources.title: arviz

research_sources.finding: DoWhy v0.14 documents explicit identifying assumptions, causal models, effect estimation, refutation, interventions, counterfactuals, and causal graphical models.
research_sources.title: DoWhy documentation

research_sources.finding: Microsoft Research describes EconML as open-source causal machine-learning software for individualized causal responses from observational or experimental data.
research_sources.title: EconML

research_sources.finding: Latest listed v0.16.0 adds sensitivity analysis for several estimators; the project states its purpose is estimating treatment effects using machine learning.
research_sources.title: EconML releases

research_sources.finding: The checked-in observer pins inspect-ai==0.3.260, sanitizes provider-secret inheritance for no-model preflight commands, and explicitly excludes HSWM execution and efficacy claims. This is an HSWM integration pin, not a claim that 0.3.260 is upstream-current.
research_sources.title: HSWM Inspect outer preflight

research_sources.finding: The release record documents an inspect_ai >=0.3.258 score-semantics change and warns that it can move reported compliance rates; evaluation versions therefore need source pinning.
research_sources.organization: UK Government BEIS / UK AI Security Institute project
research_sources.title: inspect_evals releases

research_sources.finding: Inspect documents composable datasets, agents, tools, scorers, sandboxes, over 200 pre-built evaluations, and support for arbitrary external agents.
research_sources.organization: UK AI Security Institute and Meridian Labs
research_sources.title: Inspect

research_sources.finding: PyPI lists 0.3.263 as the latest release, uploaded 2026-09-04, and records 0.3.260 as the 2026-08-21 release. HSWM's 0.3.260 pin is therefore observed but is not upstream-current.
research_sources.title: inspect-ai

research_sources.finding: Lean's official documentation describes Mathlib as enabling research and verification, cites the Polynomial Freiman-Ruzsa and Liquid Tensor projects, and describes a human-review process for contributions.
research_sources.title: Mathlib: A Foundation for Formal Mathematics Research and Verification

research_sources.finding: Documents Lean release changes and formal-proof tooling; it is evidence for the proof-assistant ecosystem, not a substitute for reviewing HSWM theorem statements and assumptions.
research_sources.title: Lean 4.22.0 release notes

research_sources.finding: The original library labels itself deprecated and directs new projects to LeanDojo-v2; its last listed release is v4.20.0.
research_sources.title: LeanDojo

research_sources.finding: Describes an end-to-end framework for training, evaluating, and deploying AI-assisted Lean 4 theorem provers; its stated installation requires Pantograph for Lean RPC.
research_sources.title: LeanDojo-v2

research_sources.finding: Describes lm-eval as an independent, reproducible, and extensible evaluation library; this is evidence of intended use, not evidence that any HSWM result generalizes.
research_sources.title: Lessons from the Trenches on Reproducible Evaluation of Language Models

research_sources.finding: Latest listed release v0.4.13 documents fixes that can change results, including few-shot evaluation-document leakage and a multiple-choice filter bug.
research_sources.title: lm-evaluation-harness releases

research_sources.finding: mathlib4 is the community-maintained Lean 4 mathematics and programming library.
research_sources.title: mathlib4

research_sources.finding: Public tasks conform to METR Task Standard and direct runners to the METR Inspect Task Bridge; publisher labels them work in progress.
research_sources.title: METR Example Task Suite

research_sources.finding: Defines a common task format with an environment, instructions, and optional automated scoring; METR reports using it for about 200 task families and about 2,000 tasks as of January 2024.
research_sources.title: METR Task Standard overview

research_sources.finding: The PyPI project lists PyMC 6.3.2; it is a probabilistic-programming tool, so posterior uncertainty is conditional on the supplied statistical model.
research_sources.title: pymc

research_sources.finding: The toolkit includes a parser, syntax checker, model checker and simulator for an executable subclass, typesetter, and PlusCal translator.
research_sources.title: TLA+ Tools

research_sources.finding: JSON-LD/schema.org-based ML dataset metadata, including resources and records; this specification is not a W3C or ISO Recommendation.
research_sources.title: Croissant specification 1.1

research_sources.finding: Google's launch documentation names Hugging Face, Kaggle and OpenML support and Dataset Search discovery; it establishes named integrations rather than comparative market share.
research_sources.title: Croissant: A metadata format for ML-ready datasets

research_sources.finding: MLCommons reports over 700,000 datasets accessible through Google Dataset Search and integrations including Hugging Face, Kaggle and OpenML; this is publisher-reported availability, not active scientific usage.
research_sources.title: Croissant working group

research_sources.finding: Searches member-deposited metadata, DOI records, funding/licensing, ORCID/ROR and post-publication updates including Retraction Watch inputs. Metadata may be incomplete; some abstracts retain copyright.
research_sources.title: Crossref REST API

research_sources.finding: Catalog metadata for datasets, distributions, data services, versions and dataset series; complements rather than replaces run provenance.
research_sources.title: Data Catalog Vocabulary 3

research_sources.finding: DCAT-AP is used to exchange European public-sector dataset descriptions; this is a concrete institutional interoperability ecosystem, not an HSWM adoption requirement.
research_sources.title: DCAT Application Profile for data portals in Europe

research_sources.finding: GQL is a published international property-graph query-language standard; ISO also lists a 2026 correction. Full paid text was not inspected and no certification claim is made.
research_sources.title: ISO/IEC 39075:2024 — GQL

research_sources.finding: Neo4j documents supported and unsupported mandatory GQL features. Cypher support must not be described as complete GQL conformance.
research_sources.title: Cypher GQL conformance

research_sources.finding: Current dated protocol revision. HSWM already tracks it in acceptance metadata; tracking official SDK pins does not mean the native SDK has been installed.
research_sources.title: Model Context Protocol revision 2026-07-28

research_sources.finding: The revision changes request-scoped protocol/capability metadata and protocol state assumptions. Adapter qualification must target the exact revision.
research_sources.title: MCP 2026-07-28 changelog

research_sources.finding: Structured scholarly discovery through a REST API; records are metadata about works and their links, not scientific verification.
research_sources.title: OpenAlex API reference

research_sources.finding: Documents linked scholarly entities; original papers and source dates are still needed to assess a scientific claim.
research_sources.title: OpenAlex data reference

research_sources.finding: Documentation observed as 1.53.0 describes Job, Run and Dataset lineage. Documentation/client release version differs from RunEvent JSON schema version.
research_sources.title: OpenLineage documentation

research_sources.finding: Facets extend core metadata with versioned schema URLs; custom HSWM facets must retain source revision and mapping boundaries.
research_sources.title: OpenLineage facets

research_sources.finding: Spark connector and documented Airflow/dbt/Flink/Spark ecosystem support integration feasibility; these are not measurements of scientific adoption.
research_sources.title: OpenLineage Spark integration

research_sources.finding: Specification observed as 1.60.0. Tracing correlates execution observations; it does not identify causal credit or independently release outcomes.
research_sources.title: OpenTelemetry Specification

research_sources.finding: GenAI semantic conventions are in a dedicated repository and labeled Development; stable core tracing does not make all GenAI attributes stable.
research_sources.title: GenAI spans semantic conventions

research_sources.finding: Entity, activity and agent provenance vocabulary supports derivation and attribution descriptions, distinct from causal identification.
research_sources.title: PROV-O

research_sources.finding: Stable RDF graph/dataset model; published syntax and semantics suites provide the interoperability test surface.
research_sources.title: RDF 1.1 Concepts

research_sources.finding: RDF 1.2 adds triple terms and other model changes. This dated snapshot is a Candidate Recommendation, not the latest final Recommendation.
research_sources.title: RDF 1.2 Concepts and Abstract Syntax

research_sources.finding: Canonical RDF dataset representation supports consistent hashing; a digest verifies bytes under the specified transform, not the truth of a claim.
research_sources.title: RDF Dataset Canonicalization 1.0

research_sources.finding: SHACL validates data graph constraints relative to a shapes graph; it does not establish scientific validity.
research_sources.title: Shapes Constraint Language

research_sources.finding: New Core draft; SHACL 1.0 remains the final Recommendation used by HSWM's existing qualification.
research_sources.title: SHACL 1.2 Core

research_sources.finding: Current draft observed one day before this scan; SPARQL 1.1 remains the latest Recommendation. A draft query feature does not justify changing HSWM's stable contract.
research_sources.title: SPARQL 1.2 Query Language

research_sources.finding: CFF 1.2.0 is YAML citation metadata for software and datasets. GitHub renders a CITATION.cff on a default branch and exposes a BibTeX snippet.
research_sources.title: Citation File Format

research_sources.finding: Version 1.2.1 specifies command-line-tool and workflow schemas/execution semantics and publishes a runner-neutral conformance-test procedure.
research_sources.title: Common Workflow Language Standards, v1.2.1

research_sources.finding: DataCite accepts several mapped formats, including DataCite XML/JSON, Schema.org JSON-LD, CodeMeta JSON, BibTeX, RIS and Citeproc JSON; crosswalks reduce but do not eliminate semantic mapping loss.
research_sources.title: DataCite supported metadata formats

research_sources.finding: Current schema version is 4.7; it defines core citation/retrieval metadata and maintained controlled vocabularies, including Project, Software and relation identifiers.
research_sources.title: DataCite Metadata Schema 4.7

research_sources.finding: DVC can retrieve data, intermediate results and models from DVC or Git repositories at a selected revision and supports remote stores.
research_sources.title: DVC command reference

research_sources.finding: The official release page identifies 3.67.1 as latest and supplies a signed release commit; any adoption must pin exact package/version and remote configuration.
research_sources.title: DVC releases

research_sources.finding: FAIR defines Findable, Accessible, Interoperable and Reusable guidance, including persistent identifiers, rich metadata, formal shared knowledge-representation languages and qualified references. It is guidance, not a conformance standard or reproducibility proof.
research_sources.title: The FAIR Guiding Principles

research_sources.finding: Official project page reports 400K+ registered users, 750K jobs per month, 22K+ citations and 150+ countries. These are project-reported service statistics, not an independently audited market measure.
research_sources.title: Galaxy Project home

research_sources.finding: Official release page marks v26.1.1 Latest and supplies a signed release commit.
research_sources.title: Galaxy v26.1.1 release

research_sources.finding: Official site lists 224+ Galaxy servers and identifies public servers hosted by Penn State/Johns Hopkins, Freiburg and Australian BioCommons infrastructure, alongside institutional and cloud deployments.
research_sources.title: Use Galaxy

research_sources.finding: Tracking records parameters, code versions, metrics and output artefacts as runs and groups them into experiments; it supports local files or a shared tracking server.

research_sources.title: Nextflow releases

research_sources.finding: Official site lists 157 institution/cluster configuration profiles, including academic and research organizations; it is concrete community deployment evidence, not a global adoption estimate.
